evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Calvin says 'Yeah, I can get you some, get you a quote worked up and emailed over. Did you have like ten minutes or so to go through it.' — no framing of a 10–15 minute time box + dependable quote promise, and no wait for a yes; jumps straight into 'what was your name'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Calvin moves immediately into 'before we jump in anything in particular about the move that you're concerned with' — this is phrased as a throwaway statement, not a genuine open-ended agenda-setting question. Destiny volunteers a concern about damage, but Calvin did not ask for it.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer did raise a concern (damage from prior movers, wanting care/wrapping), but Calvin acknowledges it ('Mm-hmm gotcha') and does not dig deeper. Only one layer touched. However, since this was never framed as a deliberate agenda question, the follow-up gap flows from the missing structure in Section 2, not a failure to probe a stated agenda.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no summary reflection offered. The concern was acknowledged but not reflected back or confirmed.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: All seven items covered: property type (apartment), floor (first floor at origin, garage at destination with four items in home), number of rooms (one bedroom confirmed), walking distance (not explicitly asked but access confirmed — 'parking lot close to the door'), additional rooms (restroom mentioned by customer), special considerations (bedroom items into home, rest into garage, all small items pre-packed), additional stops (no, single destination to brother's house).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not asked. Destiny volunteered that 'all the small things will already be packed for you guys' but Calvin never offered packing as a service.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes. 'And then are you going to have any boxes for us to move? We usually see around twenty or 25 for a one bedroom apartment.' Customer confirms small items already packed.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full. Calvin provides: hourly rate ($206/hour for two-person crew), trip fee ($70), minimum ($585 base with trip fee, 2.5 hours), and personalizes to customer's move ('You're going to be pretty close to the minimum... one bedroom usually takes about 2.5 to 3.5 hours... probably in the range of about $580 to $688').
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Calvin states: '...there is a one time trip fee of $70... everything is included in the hourly rate, so that will be all the pads and shrink wrap... insurance is included... no taxes and no credit card fees... two and a half hour minimum... We just bill in fifteen minute increments...' — transparency on fees and the 2.5-hour minimum / 15-minute increment commitment framing both present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After the estimate range is given, Calvin moves directly into the damage coverage explanation and on-time guarantee. No 'Does that feel fair?' and no silence pause.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full. 'We do have an on time guarantee if we're ever late to a window of arrival we give you, we give you money back if we don't arrive in the window that we give you.' Discount (money back) terms clearly stated.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full. 'And then we do included in our hourly rate is actually our no worries damage coverage. What that is, is just higher evaluation for your items... we actually allocate up to $2,000 per move. Just to give you peace of mind if anything got damaged we do fully resolve that.' The $2,000 limit, no deductible framing ('fully resolve'), and built-in-to-hourly-rate statement (not an add-on) all present.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. After delivering both promises, Calvin says 'But yeah, and there is an availability on Saturday October 17th...' — no version of 'Does that put those to rest?' asked, and the Two Promises are never circled back to confirm the customer's concerns (damage/care, which Destiny raised at the start) are resolved.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. 'We have all the info here needed outside of that though any other questions destiny that I can answer for you while we're on the phone.' This is the empty 'any other questions' format, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' — Destiny responds 'Nope, that was it,' which is the automatic no such throwaway phrasing invites.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Calvin never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent. The call ends with Destiny saying she wants to gather quotes and her husband will decide; Calvin responds 'I'll email you over this estimate... if you wanna move forward with that you can just send us back basically to go ahead to book it.' This is a passive wait-for-email close, not an explicit ask for the business.

top_strength: Calvin gathered comprehensive logistics details (eight furniture pieces, room-by-room layout, garage/home split at destination, pre-packed boxes) and delivered a fully anchored, personalized pricing frame ($206/hr, $70 trip fee, $585 minimum, $580–$688 range) with clear fee transparency and 2.5-hour minimum / 15-minute increment commitment framing.
coaching_note: Section 2 structure was skipped entirely — ask 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' before any probing starts, then dig two layers deep on each concern and reflect back what you heard; this would have directly addressed Destiny's damage worry and strengthened the close.
booking_note: Customer explicitly stated she needs to gather quotes and have her husband decide: 'I just want like a quote and then my husband will be the one kind of determined that and then I will be the one reaching out to like, yeah, we'll go for that.' No date/time was locked in.
